elements.evidence: "grants to Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates a non-exclusive license"

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: Grant names only "Client and ... its affiliates"; no contractor language anywhere.

elements.element: Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: No perpetual/irrevocable wording; grant remains "a non-exclusive license to use the Interface ... in accordance with this Agreement".

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No termination standard added to the grant.
"or to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets"
"upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates"

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets"

reasons: Both fallback atomic elements are satisfied in operative text: affiliate coverage conditioned on written notice inserted into the grant, and an M&A-successor exception added to the assignment consent requirement.
No preferred-only scope or duration (contractors, perpetuity, irrevocability, breach-only termination) was smuggled in, so the levels are not mixed.
Edits are surgical insertions into two existing sentences; the ordinary-course use limitation, the non-exclusivity, and Client's freedom to use alternative systems remain intact.
The successor exception rides on the pre-existing mutual assignment sentence, which is the least intrusive way to add it; no new undefined terms or dangling mechanics are created.
Preferred remains incomplete, which is acceptable at the locked fallback target and should be noted in the rationale rather than redlined further.
